lines.speaker: recruiter_sana
lines.text: Four kilometres of concrete, one patrol every twenty minutes, and nowhere to stand that isn't the road. Don't run. Running's what they're paid to notice — walking, they've got no line on the form for.

lines.speaker: recruiter_sana
lines.text: I walk this road picking people up. Not for the militia, whatever the patrol writes down about me. For a list. Who's still standing, who's got a trade, who can carry somebody who can't.

lines.speaker: recruiter_sana
lines.text: You've been on the other side of that, haven't you. It's in how you're looking at the causeway rather than down it. Don't tell me if it's bad. Just tell me if there's anyone left.

choices.text: There are people on the roofs. They held.
Eighty-four years. Be honest with them about it.

lines.speaker: recruiter_sana
lines.text: There's a swimming line up between two chimneys now, and eleven children on it most afternoons. You gave me that. I'd like to know it was worth the rope, and I think you're the only one who can tell me.

lines.speaker: recruiter_sana
lines.text: I stopped walking the road. You can't recruit people to a year — you can recruit them to a week, or to a boat, but not to eighty-four years. I tell them the date now. They go home and sit with it.
